payload.name: Extract reported interaction events with inferred topics
payload.description: During candidate extraction, when a message reports an interaction (skyped, talked, met) and mentions what was discussed or shared, create an event memory for the actor, counterpart, and inferred topic.
content: During candidate extraction, if a speaker reports a past interaction with another person (e.g., 'skyped with', 'talked to', 'met with') and mentions the subject of that interaction even indirectly, create an event candidate recording the actor, the other participant, and the topic discussed.
Attribute the action to the grammatical subject of the report; if the subject is ambiguous, prefer the speaker as the actor and note the counterpart.

When the topic is implied by a descriptor (e.g., a fan of a specific work plus 'talked characters'), store the topic as the thing discussed rather than skipping the candidate because no explicit noun phrase names it.

solves: The failure occurred because a message reporting an interaction ('skyped with a fan, talked characters') was processed but produced no extraction candidate, so the fact was never stored. The reusable mechanism is that reported interactions with contextually implied topics are memory-worthy and must become event candidates. This applies to any future message where a speaker mentions an activity with another person and the discussed/shared subject is inferable from context; it does not apply to candidate-level CRUD or to conversational filler.
